title: Encore! Encore!
desc: One-hit wonders, stage disasters & the songs that almost never happened

questions.q: 'Bohemian Rhapsody' was almost cut from the album because the label thought it was too long. How long is it?
questions.a: 5 minutes 55 seconds — the label wanted a radio-friendly single under 3 minutes

questions.q: Which band took their name from a negative review of another band's concert?
questions.a: Joy Division? No — 'Radiohead' was a Talking Heads song. But the classic answer is that 'Bad Religion' is self-descriptive. The actual one: 'The Who' chose their name partly because it was confusing and annoying to journalists

questions.q: What instrument does a Theremin use to make sound, and why is it unusual?
questions.a: It uses two antennas that detect the position of your hands — you play it without touching it

questions.q: 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' by Nirvana was named after what?
questions.a: A deodorant brand — Kurt Cobain's friend Kathleen Hanna sprayed 'Kurt smells like Teen Spirit' on his wall, and he thought it was a revolutionary slogan

questions.q: Which country has produced the most #1 Billboard Hot 100 hits per capita?
questions.a: Sweden — thanks to ABBA, Robyn, Max Martin (who wrote hits for Britney, Backstreet Boys, Taylor Swift, The Weeknd), and Avicii

questions.q: What is 'autotune' actually doing to a singer's voice, technically?
questions.a: Shifting the pitch of each note to the nearest correct semitone in real time — at extreme settings it creates the robotic effect popularised by T-Pain and Cher

questions.q: Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, Jim Morrison, Kurt Cobain, and Amy Winehouse all share what morbid coincidence?
questions.a: They all died at age 27 — the so-called '27 Club'

questions.q: The longest-running #1 single in UK chart history spent 14 weeks at the top. What was it?
questions.a: 'Stay' by The Kid LAROI and Justin Bieber? No — it was 'Old Town Road' in the US. In the UK it's 'I Believe' by Frankie Laine (1953) at 18 weeks, or more recently 'Last Christmas' by Wham! finally hit #1 in 2021

questions.q: Keith Moon of The Who was famous for destroying drum kits. What did he once drive into a swimming pool?
questions.a: A Rolls-Royce — though the more commonly verified story is a Lincoln Continental at a Holiday Inn

questions.q: What is a 'ghost note' in drumming?
questions.a: A very softly played note — barely audible but felt rhythmically, adding groove and texture between the main beats
